patch.description: Registered via a commented-out `TripRouter.route(END_POINT.UPDATE_EXPANSE).patch(acceptOrRejectExpanse)` call in trip.routes.ts, so this endpoint is not reachable at runtime. Note the path differs from the active "/update-expense" POST route above by a spelling quirk in the END_POINT.UPDATE_EXPANSE constant ("expanse" vs "expense"), so even if uncommented it would not collide with that route. post.summary: Create or progress a local refurbishment task
post.description:
Multi-step endpoint driven by the `desire` field, which selects the branch executed by `LocalRefurbishmentController`. A `checkIsTaskCompleted` pre-check runs first; if `taskId` refers to an already-completed task, the request short-circuits with a 200 "Task is completed by <name>" response instead of reaching the controller. After the branch below runs, `mutateTask` creates/updates the underlying task and lead status and returns the final response. Depending on `desire`, the shape of `localRefurbishment` and `payment` differs: - `LOCAL_REFURBISHMENT_RAISED`: creates a LocalRefurbishment document from
  `localRefurbishment[]` items `{ description, document, amount }` and links
  it to the lead.
- `LOCAL_REFURBISHMENT_APPROVED` / `LOCAL_REFURBISHMENT_REJECTED`: updates
  `EachLocalRefurbishmentSchema` items identified by
  `localRefurbishment[].refurbishmentId` using `{ refurbishmentId, status, amount }`.
- `LOCAL_REFURBISHMENT_PAYMENT_REQUEST_RAISED`: creates a Payment document
  from `payment` and updates approved items with
  `{ refurbishmentId, amount, billDocument }`, plus top-level `paymentTo`
  and `transportationCharge`.
- `LOCAL_REFURBISHMENT_PAYMENT_REJECTED`: marks `payment.paymentId` rejected. - `LOCAL_REFURBISHMENT_PAYMENT_CONFIRMED`: marks `payment.paymentId` done
  using `{ paymentId, invoiceUrl, paymentMode, paymentProcessedAt }`.
- `LOCAL_REFURBISHMENT_INSTALLATION`: updates items with
  `{ refurbishmentId, installationUrl }` and marks them `INSTALLED`.

desire.description: Target lead status; selects which branch of the controller runs.

taskId.description: Existing task id being resolved, if any.

localRefurbishmentId.description: LocalRefurbishment document id (required for approve/reject/payment-raise/installation branches).

localRefurbishment.description: Item list; required fields vary by `desire` (see description above).

payment.description: Shape varies by `desire`: payment-raise uses paymentMode/totalAmount/bank/accountHolderName/accountNo/ifsc/upiId/accountProofUrl; confirm/reject use paymentId (plus invoiceUrl/paymentMode for confirm).

200.description: Task created/updated successfully, task already completed, or journey completed with no further task (exact message/data depend on the branch taken).

patch.summary: Bulk update multiple accessory checklist items by id
patch.description: Backed by `updateCheckListsCompleteData` (registered at `PREFIX.UPDATECOMPLETECHECKLISTDATA`). NOTE — real app quirk: this route is registered on the exact same path ("/update-checklist") and HTTP method (PATCH) as the `updateCheckList` handler documented above `PREFIX.UPDATECHECKLIST`. Because both are attached via separate `router.route(...).patch(...)` calls and this one is registered second, Express effectively uses this handler for PATCH /update-checklist, shadowing `updateCheckList`. Behaviorally, this handler iterates `req.body.checkListData` (an array), applying a partial update to each identified item via `findByIdAndUpdate` with `{ new: true }` (so, unlike `updateCheckList`, the response reflects the *post*-update documents), and returns the full list of updated documents.
